start.title:
Unpaid wages?
First, find out how much
start.lead: Upload your employment contract or pay slip and we calculate what you are owed under the Labor Standards Act. You can then make a draft complaint for the labor office. No sign-up needed.
start.trust2: We do not keep your files
start.langHint: We opened in your phone's language. You can change it at the top of the screen.
start.step1: Calculate each amount you should get
start.step2: Explain in plain words which law gives you the right
start.step3: Make a draft complaint for the labor office
start.noteBody: This service is not legal advice. The result is for reference only, based on what you enter. For an exact answer, call the Ministry of Employment and Labor (1350) or ask a certified labor attorney.
start.agreeHint: Tick the box above to start

guide.title:
After you file a complaint,
this is what happens
guide.lead: Filing is free. You can file while still working there or after you leave.
guide.s1b: File online at the Labor Portal, or go to the regional labor office in charge of your workplace.
guide.s2b: When an inspector is assigned, you get a text or call.
guide.s3b: You and the employer each come in to check the facts. Bring the documents below.
guide.s4: Unpaid wages confirmed · Order to pay
guide.s4b: If unpaid wages are confirmed, the inspector orders the employer to pay by a deadline.
guide.s5b: If the employer still does not pay, you can get a document confirming the unpaid amount.
guide.s6b: With the certificate you can apply for a substitute payment from the government, or get free legal help from the Korea Legal Aid Corporation.
guide.calloutSub: Show this screen at a labor office or help center to see a Korean summary

q.nextHint: Choose or type an answer to go on
q1.title:
How many people work
at your workplace?
q1.help: Do not count the owner. Count part-time and day workers who usually work there.
q1.unsureNote: That's OK. We will count it as 5 or more and mark the result as 'estimate'.
q1.whyBody: At workplaces with fewer than 5 people, the law does not require extra pay for overtime, night or holiday work. Weekly holiday pay and severance pay do not depend on the number of workers.
q2.title: When did you start working?
q2.help: Choose the date in your contract, or your first day at work.
q2.label: Start date

Are you still
working there?
q3.help: If you left, we also calculate severance pay.

q4.title:
Choose your usual
work days and hours
q4.timeErr: The finish time must be later than the start time.
q4.sum: We will count {h} hours a day and {w} hours a week.
q4.diff: My hours were different each day
q4.diffBody: Enter start and finish times for each day in the work calendar. We then split overtime, night and holiday hours day by day.
q5.title:
What pay was
promised to you?
q5.help: Not the money you actually got, but the amount you were promised at the start.
q5.minWarn: This is less than the 2026 minimum wage (10,320 won per hour). Please check that this is the promised amount, not the money you got.
q6.title:
How much money did you get
for the unpaid month?
q6.calTitle: Add the hours you worked each day
q6.calBody: Tap a date in the calendar and enter your start and finish times. Overtime, night and holiday hours are split automatically, even when every day was different, like 10 hours a day for 4 days.

q6.calWins: For months with calendar records, we use the calendar instead of the hours below.

q6.noData: If you leave these empty, the result shows 'no information', not 0 won.

q6.night: Of these, hours between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
q6.allow: Allowance paid every month at the same amount
q6.extraHelp: If several months were unpaid, enter each month and the money you got that month. The result shows a chart by month.
q6.dup: The same month is entered twice. Please enter it once.

help.title:
Your labor office
and where to get help
help.lead: The labor office in charge depends on the address of the place you worked, not where you live.
help.loading: Loading the list of labor offices.
help.oldName: If the address uses an old name, choose the new name. If you cannot find it, tap 'Find on the Labor Portal' below.
help.noPhone: The website shows no main number. Call 1350 and ask for this office.
help.notFound: We could not confirm the office for this area. Please use 'Find on the Labor Portal'.
help.src: Checked on the Ministry of Employment and Labor website on {d}. It may have changed.
help.needCalc: The counselor page is available after you calculate.
helpn.1350: Ministry of Employment and Labor call center
helpw.1350: Questions about wages and labor law by phone. Dial 1350 with no area code. Weekdays 9:00–18:00, call charges apply. English and Chinese help: press 5.
helpw.1577-0071: Phone help for foreign workers in 17 languages. They can also help you file a complaint.
helpn.comwel: Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service (state payment)
helpw.comwel: Ask here about 'daejigeupgeum', where the state pays part of your unpaid wages first. Call charges apply.
helpw.132: If your average monthly wage is under 4 million won, you may get free help with a lawsuit for unpaid wages. Dial 132.
ready.title:
What to collect
before you complain
ready.lead: You can complain even without these. Tick what you can collect. Ticked items also appear on the counselor page.
ready.contract.h: It's OK if you don't have one. The employer must give you a written contract (Labor Standards Act Art. 17). Messages or job ads from when you started also help.
ready.payslip.h: The employer must give you a pay slip with your wages (Art. 48). Photos or screenshots are fine.
ready.bank.h: Take a screenshot in your bank app of the dates and amounts paid, or print the history.
ready.time.h: Time-clock apps, transport card history, photos from work days or your own notes. Show your work calendar too.
ready.msg.h: Text messages, KakaoTalk, recordings where they promised to pay or gave you work. Do not delete them; take screenshots.
ready.id.h: Bring it when you go to the labor office. For foreigners: alien registration card or passport.
ready.note: The more evidence you have, the faster the labor inspector can check the facts. Contact details of co-workers also help.
dj.title:
Money the state pays first:
can you look into 'daejigeupgeum'?
dj.lead: If the company does not pay, the state (Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service) may pay part of it first. A few questions tell you where to ask. We do not decide here whether you can get it or how much.
dj.paper: Did you get a 'confirmation of unpaid wages' (체불임금등·사업주 확인서) from the labor office, or a court decision (such as a payment order)?
dj.year: Did you complain to the labor office within 1 year from the day after you left? (2 years for a lawsuit)
dj.yearNow: Did you complain to the labor office within 1 year from the day after your last unpaid payday? (2 years for a lawsuit)
dj.closed: Did the company go bankrupt, start rehabilitation, or close in practice?
dj.a.filing: Not yet, my complaint is in progress
dj.r.simple: You can look into the 'simple daejigeupgeum'. Claim it from the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service within 6 months from the date you got the confirmation (1 year from a final court decision).
dj.r.filing: When your complaint ends and you get the confirmation of unpaid wages, you can look into the simple daejigeupgeum. You must claim within 6 months from the date you got it.
dj.r.first: The simple daejigeupgeum needs a confirmation from the labor office or a court decision. Please complain to the labor office first.
dj.r.employed: If you still work there, your hourly ordinary wage at the time must be below 1.1 times that year's minimum wage, and you can get it only once per company.
dj.r.year: If more than 1 year has passed, or you are not sure, it may be difficult. Please ask the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service (1588-0075).
dj.r.closed: If the company got a bankruptcy or rehabilitation decision, or the labor office recognizes it as closed in practice, you can also look into the 'insolvency daejigeupgeum'. Claim at the labor office within 2 years from the decision.
dj.r.closedEmployed: The insolvency daejigeupgeum is only for people who have left.
dj.r.company: Conditions about the company (industrial accident insurance, in business for more than 6 months) are checked by the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service.
dj.callSub: Ask if you can get it and what papers you need
dj.note: Plain-language summary of official guidance (checked 15 Nov 2026). The service decides whether you can get it and how much.
words.title:
Difficult words,
made simple
words.lead: Tap any underlined word on the screens to see the same explanation.
words.src: Laws were checked on law.go.kr on 15 Nov 2026. This is not legal advice.
w.ordinaryWage.d: The pay you always get for your working hours: basic pay plus allowances paid at the same amount every month. Overtime, night and holiday pay are calculated from it.
w.averageWage.d: The money you got in the 3 months before leaving, divided by the number of days in that period. Severance pay is based on it. If it is lower than the ordinary wage, the ordinary wage is used.
w.weeklyHoliday.d: One paid day off a week if you worked all your set days that week. Not given if you agreed to work fewer than 15 hours a week.
w.overtime.d: Hours worked over 8 a day or 40 a week. At workplaces with 5 or more people, you get 50% extra for these hours.
w.night.d: Hours worked between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. At workplaces with 5 or more people, you get 50% extra.
w.holidayWork.d: Hours worked on a day off. At workplaces with 5 or more people: 50% extra up to 8 hours, 100% extra after 8 hours. These hours are not added again as overtime.
w.severance.d: Money you get when you leave after working more than 1 year: at least 30 days of average wage for each year. Not given for less than 1 year or under 15 hours a week.
w.minWage.d: The lowest pay per hour set by the government. In 2026 it is 10,320 won. Even if you agreed to less, you must get at least this.
w.underFive.d: A place where fewer than 5 people usually work. Extra pay for overtime, night and holiday work is not required, but wages, weekly holiday pay, severance pay and minimum wage still apply.
w.complaint.d: Telling the labor office that you were not paid so they check it. It is free, and you can do it while working there or after you left. Wage claims end after 3 years, so do not wait.
w.laborOffice.d: A local office of the Ministry of Employment and Labor that receives and investigates complaints. The office in charge depends on your workplace address.
w.daeji.d: When the company does not pay, the state (Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service) pays part of it first and collects it from the company later.
